transcript.text: Thanks Noor. I appreciate your recommendations, especially the point about the chair role potentially creating the same concern I observed. Here are my recommendations. For membership: I strongly agree with non-managerial staff from both combined groups, and I'd add that we should ensure no participant's direct manager is in the room at all — not as a member, not as an observer, not as a facilitator. Based on what I've seen, even the physical presence of a direct manager suppresses participation. For operating format: I support monthly meetings for the first several months and the anonymous written question channel Maya's policy requires. I'd also recommend that employees be able to submit concerns through the anonymous channel without attending meetings at all, so nobody is forced into a group setting they're not comfortable with. Regarding Noor's chair role: I think a neutral external facilitator is the safest option. If that's not feasible, a rotational chair drawn from non-managerial staff — with no one chairing a session where their own direct reports are present — would be my second choice. For safeguards: Beyond what Noor outlined, I recommend an explicit ground rule that any manager who shows up unannounced to a council meeting will be asked to leave, and that participation is strictly voluntary with no retaliation. I also support anonymized, aggregated summaries to you, Priya. No individual-level comments should reach anyone's manager. Finally, I'd ask that the council's existence and the anonymous channel be communicated to all staff in a way that doesn't go through the management chain — perhaps directly from your office, Priya — so employees know this isn't a manager-controlled process.
